verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:
verses.commentary:
12:1 This is a textual marker of inspiration.

SPECIAL TOPIC: INSPIRATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: WAYS OF REVELATION

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你住在悖逆的家中。他们有眼睛看不见，有耳朵听不见，因为他们是悖逆之家。
verses.en: “Son of man, you are living in the midst of a rebellious house.[NOTE:1] They have eyes to see, but do not see, and ears to hear, but do not hear,[NOTE:2] because they are a rebellious house.
notes: The book of Ezekiel frequently refers to the Israelites as a rebellious house (Ezek 2:5, 6, 8; 3:9, 26-27; 12:2-3, 9, 25; 17:12; 24:3).
This verse is very similar to Isa 6:9-10.
verses.commentary:
12:2 "you live in the midst of the rebellious house" Shockingly, this described the covenant people living
and worshiping in Jerusalem (cf. Ezek. 2:5,7,8; 3:7; 20:8; Isa. 6:5,9-13; 29:13).

▣ "who have eyes to see but do not see, who have ears to hear but do not hear" Spiritual blindness and
deafness has always been a problem for the children of Jacob (cf. Deut. 29:1-4; 32:5; Isa. 1:2-3; 6:9,10;
Jer. 5:21; 6:10; Zech. 7:11; Matt. 13:13, 14; Mark 8:18; John 9:39-41; 12:39-40; Acts 28:26, 27) and all
fallen humanity in general! The results of Eden are pervasive!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE FALL OF MANKIND

verses.zh: 所以人子啊，你要预备掳去使用的物件，在白日当他们眼前从你所住的地方移到别处去；他们虽是悖逆之家，或者可以揣摩思想。
verses.en: “Therefore, son of man, pack up your belongings as if for exile. During the day, while they are watching, pretend to go into exile. Go from where you live to another place. Perhaps they will understand,[NOTE:1] although they are a rebellious house.
notes: Heb “see.” This plays on the uses of “see” in v. 2. They will see his actions with their eyes and perhaps they will “see” with their mind, that is, understand or grasp the point.
verses.commentary:
12:3-6 This describes in dramatic symbolism the fall of Jerusalem brought about by Nebuchadneaazr's
army in 586 B.C.

12:3 "son of man" See note at Ezek. 2:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SON OF MAN

▣ "prepare for yourself baggage for exile" Ezekiel is to pack bags as if he were being exiled
(he had done this very thing in 597 B.C.). The VERB
(BDB 793, KB 889) is the first of two Qal IMPERTAIVES.

▣ "go into exile" This VERB's (BDB 162, KB 191) basic meaning is
"to uncover" or "to remove," but here it is used for going into exile (cf. Jdg. 18:30; 2 Kgs. 17:23; 25:21;
Isa. 5:13; Jer. 1:3; 52:27; Lam. 1:3; Ezek. 12:3; 39:23; Amos 1:5; 5:5; 6:7; 7:11,17; Micah 1:16).
It is the second Qal IMPERATIVE.

▣ "by day in their sight" "In their sight" (BDB 744) is repeated twice for emphasis. It
is a wordplay on their blindness mentioned in Ezek. 12:2.

This wordplay continues in the phrase "perhaps they will understand," which is literally the
verb "to see" (BDB 906, KB 1157, Qal IMPERFECT).

Some modern theologians have taken literary phrases like this and Jer. 26:3; 36:3,7 and have
asserted that YHWH does not know how free moral human agents will act. It is called "Open Theism." In my
opinion all truth comes in tension-filled pairs. There are theological ditches on both sides. In this case
the two extremes are

- God's sovereignty chose some to heaven and others to hell (no human choice at all)

- Human choice is ultimate and free and unknown by God (human choice is the deciding factor)

Our text is a literary statement, not a theological doctrine! YHWH desires that none should
perish (cf. Ezek. 18:30-32), but He requires a repentant, faithful human response.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE BIBLE IN EASTERN LITERATURE (biblical paradoxes)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 你要在白日当他们眼前带出你的物件去，好像预备掳去使用的物件。到了晚上，你要在他们眼前亲自出去，像被掳的人出去一样。
verses.en: Bring out your belongings packed for exile during the day while they are watching. And go out at evening, while they are watching, as if for exile.

verses.zh: 你要在他们眼前挖通了墙，从其中将物件带出去。
verses.en: While they are watching, dig a hole in the wall and carry your belongings out through it.
verses.commentary:
12:5 "Dig a hole through the wall" This refers to the wall of his house, which was made of dried bricks (little wood was
available in southern Mesopotamia). Obviously Ezekiel's activity caught the people's attention. The noise of breaking through the
walls right after dark (cf. Ezek. 12:4,6) caused quite a disturbance.

The VERB "dig" (BDB 369, KB 365) is the third Qal IMPERATIVE in this
context. Ezekiel's dramatic actions were not his own design, but YHWH's (cf. Ezek. 12:6,7). This action mimicked the siege techniques
of the Neo-Babylonian army in Jerusalem.

verses.zh: 到天黑时，你要当他们眼前搭在肩头上带出去，并要蒙住脸看不见地，因为我立你作以色列家的预兆。」
verses.en: While they are watching, raise your baggage onto your shoulder and carry it out in the dark.[NOTE:1] You must cover your face so that you cannot see the ground[NOTE:2] because I have made you an object lesson[NOTE:3] to the house of Israel.”
notes: Apart from this context the Hebrew term occurs only in Gen 15:17, in reference to the darkness after sunset. It may mean twilight.
verses.commentary:
12:6 "in the dark" This rare term (BDB 759, KB 832) occurs only here and Gen. 15:17. Both occur in visions.

- Genesis 15, of YHWH removing Canaanites from Canaan because of their sin and giving the land to Israel

- Ezekiel 12, of YHWH about to remove the remaining Judeans from Jerusalem

▣ "You shall cover your face so that you shall not see the land, for I have set you as a sign before the house of Israel"
This probably relates to King Zedekiah (called "the prince" in vv. 10,12) who attempted escape from Jerusalem during the neo-Babylonian
siege (cf. 2 Kgs. 25:1-7; Jer. 39:4), as do Ezek. 12:10 and 12. He was caught and blinded by Nebuchadnezzar II at Riblah (cf. Ezek. 12:13).

For the covenant people there were two things which they depended on

- YHWH's covenant promises about Jerusalem (Deuteronomy and Isaiah)

- YHWH's promises about a Davidic king (2 Samuel 7; 1 Chronicles 17)

For both of these to be taken and destroyed was a theological blow that was unimaginable for them.
They had forgotten the conditional nature of all the covenant promises!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED MONARCHY

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

verses.zh: 我就照着所吩咐的去行，白日带出我的物件，好像预备掳去使用的物件。到了晚上，我用手挖通了墙。天黑的时候，就当他们眼前搭在肩头上带出去。
verses.en: So I did just as I was commanded. I carried out my belongings packed for exile during the day, and at evening I dug myself a hole through the wall with my hands. I went out in the darkness, carrying my baggage[NOTE:1] on my shoulder while they watched.
notes: The words “my baggage” are not in the Hebrew text but are implied from the context.

verses.zh: 次日早晨，耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me in the morning:
verses.commentary: 12:8 YHWH communicated to Ezekiel regularly as he performed the previous revelation.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，以色列家，就是那悖逆之家，岂不是问你说：『你做什么呢？』
verses.en: “Son of man, has not the house of Israel, that rebellious house, said to you, ‘What are you doing?’
verses.commentary:
12:9 "the rebellious house" This phrase refers to the exiles (cf. Ezek. 2:5-8). The term "rebellion"
(BDB 598) is used often by Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 2:5,6,7,8; 3:9,26; 12:2 [twice], 3,9,25; 17:12; 23:3; 44:6).

verses.zh: 你要对他们说：『主耶和华如此说：这是关乎耶路撒冷的君王和他周围以色列全家的预表（原文是担子）。』
verses.en: Say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: The prince will raise this burden in Jerusalem,[NOTE:1] and all the house of Israel within it.’[NOTE:2]
notes: The prince in Jerusalem refers to King Zedekiah. The Hebrew termנָשִׂיא (nasi’, “leader, chief prince”) refers to one lifted up and here means the leader of Jerusalem. The idea in the message is: “As goes the king, so goes the city.” The fortunes of the city are bound up in and symbolized by the king.tc The MT reads: “The prince, the load/oracle, this, in Jerusalem.” The term מַשָּׂא (massaʾ) may refer to a “burden” or prophetic “oracle” (the two homonyms also coming from the same root, cf. Isa 13:1). Also the preposition ב (bet) can mean “in” or “against.” The Targum says, “Concerning the prince is this oracle,” assuming the addition of a preposition. The LXX reads the word for “burden” as a synonym for leader, as both words are built on the same root, but the result does not make good sense in context. The current translation assumes that the verb יִשָּׂא (yisaʾ) from the root נָשָׂא (nasaʾ) has dropped out due to homoioteleuton (cf. vv. 7 and 12 for the verb). The original text would have three consecutive words based on the root נָשָׂא and an environment conducive to an omission in copying: הַנָּשִׂיא יִשָּׂא הַמַּשָּׂא הַזֶּה (hannasiʾ yissaʾ hammassaʾ hazzeh, “the prince will raise this burden”). Another possibility is that הַנָּשִׂיא is an inadvertent addition based on v. 12, so that the text should be “[This is] the oracle against…,” but the formula typically uses the construct state to mean “the oracle about…,” and this would be the only case where Ezekiel uses this term for an oracle. It is also unlikely that this is a copulative sentence, “The prince is the oracle.” While Hebrew can make copulative sentences without a verb, it is odd to do so with articular nouns. The sequence article + noun + article + noun is normally: a case where the second term is an adverbial accusative of place or time, a case where the second term acts as an adjective, part of a list, a case of apposition, or an improper construct chain (or other textual issue involving one of the apparent articles). Besides this verse, only Jer 4:26 (הַכַּרְמֶל הַמִּדְבָּר, hakkarmel hammidbar, “Carmel is/had become a wilderness”) may be suggested as a place where this syntax makes a copulative sentence, but there the first word should be understood as a proper noun. Also if the syntax were this simple (“the A is the B”), one would have expected the versions to follow it.
The MT reads “within them.” Possibly a scribe copied this form from the following verse “among them,” but only “within it” makes sense in this context.
verses.commentary:
12:10 "Say to them" This (BDB 55; KB 65) Qal INFINITIVE is repeated twice (Ezek. 12:10 and Ezek. 12:11)
to emphasize that Ezekiel is modeling the future judgment of YHWH on idolatrous Jerusalem.

verses.zh: 你要说：『我作你们的预兆：我怎样行，他们所遭遇的也必怎样，他们必被掳去。』
verses.en: Say, ‘I am an object lesson[NOTE:1] for you. Just as I have done, so it will be done to them; they will go into exile and captivity.’
notes: object lesson is מוֹפֵת (mofet, “wonder, sign”), which here refers to a sign or portent of bad things to come.
verses.commentary:
12:11 "a sign" This term (BDB 69) basically means "wonder," "sign," or "portent." Here it is used to show YHWH's control of
future events (i.e. Ezek. 12:6,11; 24:24,27; 1 Kgs. 13:3,5; 2 Chr. 32:24;31). In the Ancient Near East a military defeat demonstrated the
power of one national god over another. Israel was defeated because of her covenant disobedience, not YHWH's impotence! Passages
such as this demonstrate His omnipotence and control!

SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGN (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: BIBLE (its uniqueness and inspiration)

▣ "As I have done, so it will be done to them" Notice these are words from YHWH for Ezekiel to
speak to the exiles. They show

- the power of YHWH's word (cf. Isa. 44:24-28; 45:23; 55:11; Matt. 24:35)

- that Ezekiel is a true prophet (i.e. his prophecies came true)

Both of these theological items are crucial, especially when Ezekiel begins to prophesy about the restoration!

▣ "they will go into exile, into captivity" The "they" refers to the few in Judah and Jerusalem who will escape the
destruction and horror of the invasion (cf. Ezek. 12:16).

The terms "exile" (BDB 163) and "captivity" (BDB 985) are parallel. Judgment is coming! YHWH will do it! His
own people will be taken out of the land (cf. Jer. 13:19; 15:2; 20:4,6) which He promised to their fathers! YHWH is no respecter of
persons. He removed the evil Canaanites (cf. Gen. 15:12-22), now He will remove evil Judah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

verses.zh: 他们中间的君王也必在天黑的时候将物件搭在肩头上带出去。他们要挖通了墙，从其中带出去。他必蒙住脸，眼看不见地。
verses.en: “The prince[NOTE:1] who is among them will raise his belongings[NOTE:2] onto his shoulder in darkness and will go out. He[NOTE:3] will dig a hole in the wall to leave through. He will cover his face so that he cannot see the land with his eyes.
notes: The prince is a reference to Zedekiah.
The words “his belongings” are not in the Hebrew text but are implied.
The MT reads “they”; the LXX and Syriac read “he.”
verses.commentary:
12:12 "They will dig a hole" This refers to the attendants (cf. v. 4) of Zedekiah, who apparently dug a
secret hole in the wall of Jerusalem for the king to secretly escape.

Surprisingly, the LXX and Peshitta, followed by the RSV and NRSV, have "he." The UBS Text
Project, p. 33, gives "they" a "B" rating. It is simply a literary way of referring to Zedekiah and his entourage (cf. v. 14).

verses.zh: 我必将我的网撒在他身上，他必在我的网罗中缠住。我必带他到迦勒底人之地的巴比伦；他虽死在那里，却看不见那地。
verses.en: But I will throw my net over him, and he will be caught in my snare. I will bring him to Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans[NOTE:1] (but he will not see it),[NOTE:2] and there he will die.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “Babylonians” (NCV, NLT). sn The Chaldeans were a group of people in the country south of Babylon from which Nebuchadnezzar came. The Chaldean dynasty his father established became the name by which the Babylonians are regularly referred to in the book of Jeremiah, while Jeremiah’s contemporary, Ezekiel, uses both terms.
He will not see it. This prediction was fulfilled in 2 Kgs 25:7 and Jer 52:11, which recount how Zedekiah was blinded before being deported to Babylon.
There he will die. This was fulfilled when King Zedekiah died in exile (Jer 52:11).
verses.commentary:
12:13 "I shall also spread My net over him" This refers to the capture of King Zedekiah. It was YHWH who
planned and executed (by means of the Neo-Babylonian army) his capture (i.e. 5:10,12; 6:8; 12:14,15; 20:23; 22:15;
36:19).

The imagery used is for a "net" (BDB 440, cf. Ezek. 17:20; 19:8), which denotes either

- a fishing net

- casting, Ezek. 12:13; 32:3

- dragging, Ezek. 26:5,14; 47:10

- a snare (for birds)

▣ "the Chaldeans" See SPECIAL TOPIC: CHALDEANS

▣ "yet he will not see it" See 2 Kgs. 25:1-7; Jer. 39:1-10, especially Ezek. 12:7. Zedekiah will be blinded by Nebuchadnezzar, just
after his failed attempt to escape.

▣ "he will die there" The blinded and exiled Davidic King Zedekiah will die in captivity (cf. Jer. 52:11).

The king that would not "see" now can not "see" (cf. Isa. 6:9-13). The result of his faithless reign was destruction and exile (cf. Jeremiah 39).

verses.zh: 周围一切帮助他的和他所有的军队，我必分散四方（方：原文是风），也要拔刀追赶他们。
verses.en: All his retinue—his attendants and his troops—I will scatter to every wind; I will unleash a sword behind them.
verses.commentary:
12:14

NASB, NRSV, JPSOA, LXX
"his helpers"

NKJV, Peshitta
"to help him"

TEV
"all the members of his court and

his advisers and bodyguards"

NJB
"his army"

REB
"body guard"

The UBS Text Project, p. 34, mentions:

- the MT has "his guard" (עזרה, BDB 740 I, MASCULINE NOUN)

- the Massoretic scholars suggested (Qere) "his help" (עזרו, BDB 740 I, FEMININE NOUN)

SPECIAL TOPIC: MASORETIC TEXT

▣ "I shall scatter to every wind" This VERB (BDB 279, KB
280, Piel IMPERFECT) is used in Ezek. 5:2, which describes
Ezekiel's prophetic acts of judgment (see note at Ezek. 12:13).

"Every wind" is an idiom for every direction (i.e. complete exile).

verses.zh: 我将他们四散在列国、分散在列邦的时候，他们就知道我是耶和华。
verses.en: “Then they will know that I am the Lord when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them among foreign countries.
verses.commentary:
12:15 This verse, which describes the exile of Judah into all the surrounding nations, can be viewed theologically in two ways.

- This is the consequence of covenant rebellion predicted in Deuteronomy (i.e. Deut. 4:27; 28:64; 29:28).

- This had a secondary effect of forcing Israel to fulfill her missionary mandate (similar to the dispersion of the Tower
of Babel). Ezekiel makes this missionary mandate definite in Ezek. 36:20-21, 22-38!

▣ "they will know" This VERB (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT) is used in a special
sense in Ezekiel. It describes YHWH's desire that His people, all people, know (in the sense of intimate personal relationship, i.e. Gen. 4:1; Jer. 1:5)
Him. The characteristic phrase "they will know that I am the Lord" first occurs in the covenant context of the exodus
(cf. Exod. 6:7; 7:5,17; 16:12; 29:46). The phrase refers to future actions of YHWH, positive and negative. All His acts are revelations of His character and purposes!

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

verses.zh: 我却要留下他们几个人得免刀剑、饥荒、瘟疫，使他们在所到的各国中述说他们一切可憎的事，人就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: But I will let a small number of them survive the sword, famine, and pestilence, so that they can confess all their abominable practices to the nations where they go. Then they will know that I am the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
12:16 "But I will spare a few of them" The VERB (BDB 451,
KB 451, Hiphil PERFECT) is used in several senses by Ezekiel.

- spare, Ezek. 6:8; 12:16

- the rest, Ezek. 34:18

- some survivors, Ezek. 14:22

- what remains, Ezek. 39:14,28; 48:15,18,21

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, three senses.

▣ "the sword, the famine, the pestilence" These are the three major enemies of a city under siege
(cf. Ezek. 5:12; 6:11-12; 7:15; 14:21). These are mentioned repeatedly in Deuteronomy (esp. Deuteronomy 27-29).

▣ "and may know that I am the Lord" The goal of a "chosen people"
was to be a means of revelation to the nations. Israel was called to be a kingdom of priests (cf. Exod. 19:5-6),
but she failed.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你吃饭必胆战，喝水必惶惶忧虑。
verses.en: “Son of man, eat your bread with trembling[NOTE:1] and drink your water with anxious shaking.
notes: The Hebrew term normally refers to an earthquake (see 1 Kgs 19:11; Amos 1:1).
verses.commentary:
12:18 Ezekiel is told to emulate the fear of the people of Judah facing invasion (cf. Ezek. 12:19;
Deut. 28:65).

- eat bread with trembling (BDB 950)

- drink water

- with quivering (BDB 919)

- with anxiety (BDB 178)

It is possible that this is a reversal of the Exodus meal (cf. Exodus 11-12)! YHWH gave them the land
(cf. Gen. 15:12-21), but now He takes it away!

verses.zh: 你要对这地的百姓说：主耶和华论耶路撒冷和以色列地的居民如此说，他们吃饭必忧虑，喝水必惊惶。因其中居住的众人所行强暴的事，这地必然荒废，一无所存。
verses.en: Then say to the people of the land, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says about the inhabitants of Jerusalem and of the land of Israel: They will eat their bread with anxiety and drink their water in fright, for their land will be stripped bare of all it contains because of the violence of all who live in it.
verses.commentary:
12:19 "the people of the land" In the earlier parts of the OT this phrase means the landed nobility,
but after the exile and in Jesus' day it speaks of the poorest people of the land. Here it refers to Ezekiel's
fellow exiles.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PEOPLE OF THE LAND

verses.zh: 有居民的城邑必变为荒场，地也必变为荒废；你们就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: The inhabited towns will be left in ruins, and the land will be devastated. Then you will know that I am the Lord.’”
verses.commentary:
12:20 Two terms describe YHWH's judgment of Judah.

- the VERB "will be laid waste," BDB 351,
KB 349, Qal IMPERFECT, cf. Ezek. 6:6; 25:19; 30:7

- the NOUN "desolation," BDB 1031, cf. Ezek. 6:14; 14:15,16; 15:8; 23:33;
also used often in the prophecies against the nations, chapters 25-32

verses.zh: 耶和华的话临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:
verses.commentary:
12:21-25 There are two stated reasons why the exiles were holding out hope that Jerusalem would not fall
and that they might return.

- Ezekiel's prophecies were far into the future and would not affect them, Ezek. 12:22-23,26-28.

- There were other prophets who were predicting the opposite of Jeremiah and Ezekiel.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，在你们以色列地怎么有这俗语，说『日子迟延，一切异象都落了空』呢？
verses.en: “Son of man, what is this proverb you have in the land of Israel, ‘The days pass slowly, and every vision fails’?
verses.commentary:
12:22 "the days are long and every vision fails" This was a proverb spoken by the rebellious house
of Israel (cf. Ezek. 12:27) that God was not going to fulfill His prophecy through Ezekiel. Ezekiel
started preaching in the fifth year of the exile and the city of Jerusalem did not fall until the thirteenth
year of the exile. Delay does not mean YHWH's word will not be accomplished (cf. Ezek. 12:23,25,28).
Ezekiel often quotes (or alludes to) popular proverbs (cf. Ezek. 16:44; 18:2,3) or parables
(cf. Ezek. 17:2; 24:3).

verses.zh: 你要告诉他们说：『主耶和华如此说：我必使这俗语止息，以色列中不再用这俗语。』你却要对他们说：『日子临近，一切的异象必都应验。』
verses.en: Therefore tell them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: I hereby end this proverb; they will not recite it in Israel any longer.’ But say to them, ‘The days are at hand when every vision will be fulfilled.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “the days draw near, and the word of every vision (draws near).”

verses.zh: 从此，在以色列家中必不再有虚假的异象和奉承的占卜。
verses.en: For there will no longer be any false visions or flattering omens amidst the house of Israel.
verses.commentary:
12:24 "false" See SPECIAL TOPIC: EMPTY, VAIN, FALSE, NOTHINGNESS

▣ "divination" This (BDB 890) was strictly forbidden for the people of God. It is an attempt by
humans to know and control future events! The fact that a prophet would use this forbidden method to know God's
will shows the degradation of the leadership (cf. Lev. 19:26; Deut. 18:10-12; Ezek. 13:6,7,9,23; 21:21,22,23,29;
22:28; Jer. 14:14). For an interesting discussion of occult practices in the OT see Synonyms of
the Old Testament by Robert G. Girdlestone, pp. 296-302, and Dictionary of Biblical Imagery, pp. 608-610.

SPECIAL TOPIC: DIVINATION

SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC

verses.zh: 我―耶和华说话，所说的必定成就，不再耽延。你们这悖逆之家，我所说的话必趁你们在世的日子成就。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: For I, the Lord, will speak. Whatever word I speak will be accomplished. It will not be delayed any longer. Indeed in your days, O rebellious house, I will speak the word and accomplish it, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”
verses.commentary:
12:25 "'I shall speak the word and perform it,' declares the Lord God" Also note Ezek. 6:10; 12:28;
17:24; 22:14; Isa. 14:24; 55:6-13. YHWH's word is sure (i.e. Isa. 55:9-11), but often His patience and longsuffering are misunderstood.

verses.zh: 耶和华的话又临到我说：
verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:
verses.commentary: 12:26-28 See note at Ezek. 12:21-25.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，以色列家的人说：『他所见的异象是关乎后来许多的日子，所说的预言是指着极远的时候。』
verses.en: “Take note, son of man, the house of Israel is saying, ‘The vision that he sees is for distant days; he is prophesying about the far future.’

verses.zh: 所以你要对他们说：『主耶和华如此说：我的话没有一句再耽延的，我所说的必定成就。这是主耶和华说的。』」
verses.en: Therefore say to them, ‘This is what the Sovereign Lord says: None of my words will be delayed any longer! The word I speak will come to pass, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

1Then the word of the Lord came to me, saying, 2"Son
of man, you live in the midst of the rebellious house, who have eyes to see but do not see, ears to hear but do not hear; for they are a rebellious house.

place in their sight. Perhaps they will understand though they are a rebellious house. 4Bring your baggage out by day in their sight, as baggage for exile.
Then you will go out at evening in their sight, as those going into exile. 5Dig a hole through the wall in their sight and go out through it. 6Load
the baggage on your shoulder in their sight and carry it out in the dark. You shall cover your face so that you cannot see the land, for I have
set you as a sign to the house of Israel."
